A colossal dead capital-ship hull drifts through deep space, its kilometers of scarred plating dark and cold, weapon batteries silent, a vast breach torn through the midsection trailing frozen debris in a long glittering arc.
A silent station corridor, every panel long dead, ribbed bulkheads laced with frost, severed cables coiling slowly in the still air, a hatch at the far end hanging half-open on a bent hinge.

A ghostly command bridge, every console dark and dusted, the captain's chair turned away and empty, star charts still pinned to a dead screen, the cracked viewport showing a slow-wheeling field of stars.

A vast wrecked hangar bay, a shuttle collapsed nose-first across the deck, one wing sheared away, a single helmet drifting in the frozen air, the enormous bay doors seized half-open on buckled tracks.
A cold reactor chamber, the great core dead and rimed with frost, warning lights long extinguished, coolant pipes burst and refrozen into jagged crystalline sprays along the chamber walls.

A cargo hold packed with sealed containers drifted loose from their racks, tumbling in slow silence, frost blooming across every surface, a broken pallet spinning lazily in the center of the dark space.

The exterior of a cruiser snapped cleanly in half, both sections tumbling apart in slow counter-rotation, wiring and conduit trailing between them like torn sinew, the exposed cross-sections gaping into vacuum.

A crashed wreck half-buried in an asteroid's grey regolith, one engine nacelle sheared off and lying meters away, the hull buckled and blackened, a gaping rent along the spine packed with drifted grey dust.

An engineering deck choked floor to ceiling with tangled cabling, pulled loose from conduits lining every wall, the mass hanging motionless in the dead air, a single spanner frozen mid-fall near a corroded access panel.

A medical bay, gurneys drifting free of their floor locks, restraint straps trailing, empty IV lines swaying gently, every cabinet hanging open, instruments scattered across the cold deck in long-settled silence.
An observation dome cracked open to vacuum, the transparent panel split and frosted at its edges, stars visible through the gap, loose debris and a single data-pad frozen at the break point.

A tight airlock chamber between two derelict sections, both inner and outer doors cycled open and dead, frost coating every handhold, the status panel blank, a torn pressure suit sleeve caught in the outer seal.

A docking ring with a smaller derelict still clamped to its berth, the umbilical conduit collapsed between them, both hulls dark and cold, the clamps locked permanently shut around the other vessel's corroded collar.

A spiral stairwell in zero-gravity, every step a surface for drifting refuse, floating scraps of paper, a broken mug, a single boot turning slowly as it ascends through the dark shaft without destination.
The exterior of a dead station, its ring sections no longer rotating, solar arrays folded and dark, a cluster of antennae bent and cold, one docking arm snapped off and drifting fifty meters out.
A narrow crawlspace between hull layers, insulation torn from the walls, frost crystals thick on every pipe, a dead helmet-lamp lodged in the conduit ahead, the passage tapering into absolute black.
A crew mess hall, trays drifting among overturned chairs, a sealed ration pack frozen to a tabletop, every light fitting dark, frost rimming the viewport that looks out onto unbroken, uncaring stars.

A sensor array gallery along the outer hull, instrument housings smashed or split open, wiring dangling from each mounting bracket, the long curved catwalk ending at a section torn completely away into space.

A weapons turret bay, the twin barrels locked at a downward angle, ammunition feeds ruptured and empty, the gunner's seat frosted solid, targeting displays shattered and dark, the turret sealed in permanent stillness.

A long pressurized corridor connecting two station modules, its midpoint buckled inward by an old impact, debris piled against the crease, both blast doors at either end sealed shut by the same dead system.

The exterior of a dead frigate from close off the bow, its running lights cold and black, hull plating warped by ancient heat, the forward sensor cluster gone entirely, the bare mounting ring staring like an empty socket.

A personnel quarters block, six bunks folded against the walls in a tight cabin, personal effects drifting free, a photograph sealed in cold plastic turning slowly near the ceiling, every surface sheeted in frost.

A fuel transfer junction, three wide conduits meeting at a central manifold, all valves open and corroded in place, a slow glitter of frozen propellant crystals still drifting from a ruptured line long since bled dry.

A secondary bridge or combat information center, smaller than the main, every chair anchored but empty, a tactical display housing cracked open and dark, loose data-chips scattered across the cold floor in long-settled disorder.

A tight exterior maintenance alcove on the hull's underside, tool brackets empty, a single tether clip still locked to a rung, the surrounding plating scorched and pitted, the alcove open on one side to silent, lightless space.
